html:
Euromaidan was a wave of protests in Ukraine that began on Kyiv's Maidan Nezalezhnosti, Independence Square, on 21 November 2013, after President Viktor Yanukovych dropped a planned agreement with the European Union.

The beating of students on 30 November brought hundreds of thousands into the streets, and protesters held the square through the winter. Harsh laws against protest in January led to clashes. Between 18 and 20 February 2014 about a hundred people, honoured as the Heavenly Hundred, and some police were killed, many by snipers. Yanukovych fled to Russia on 21 February, and parliament removed him. Ukrainians call it the Revolution of Dignity. Russia called it a coup and within days began the seizure of Crimea and backed fighting in Donbas. It followed the Orange Revolution of 2004.
sum: Euromaidan was a wave of protests in Ukraine that began on Kyiv's Maidan Nezalezhnosti, Independence Square, on 21 November 2013, after President Viktor Yanukovych dropped a planned agreement with the European Union.
